_about: The story of each version: its theme, what it feels like day to day, what it contemplates and why. Written from docs/research/plan-doc (01-the-plan, 02-why-each-stay-is-this-long, 03-what-were-missing) and the region guides. Stay notes say why a base gets that many nights in that version.

plan.theme: Snow country, crab season and a ryokan New Year
plan.tagline: Six bases, two or more nights everywhere, light afternoons.
plan.feel: An easy start in Tokyo while the jet lag wears off and the four first-timers get the classic days. Then the Hokuriku shinkansen to Kanazawa for the slow middle of the trip: a whole house with a kitchen and a washing machine, crab at its peak, the snow-roped pines of Kenroku-en, museums done by the 27th before they close. A bus over the mountains through Shirakawa-go's thatched farmhouses to Takayama's old town, then a 45-minute train down the valley to Gero to sit out the busiest travel days of the year in a ryokan: footbaths, kaiseki on New Year's Eve, the temple bell at midnight, a New Year breakfast. New Year's Day is the quiet day to travel, so that is when we go to Kyoto. Temples and the New Year rituals there, Nara's deer on the Monday when museums close, then a private open-air bath in Hakone with two dawns to catch Fuji clear, and two last Tokyo days for the museums that were shut in December.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji and the Hama-rikyu garden, Meiji Jingu and the Nezu Museum, Asakusa, a free Fuji viewpoint, the illuminations
Kanazawa: Kenroku-en with the yukitsuri snow ropes, the castle park, the 21st Century Museum, Higashi Chaya and a gold-leaf workshop, the samurai house, Omicho market and kobako crab
Shirakawa-go: the thatched village in snow, on the bus between Kanazawa and Takayama
Takayama: the Jinya before it closes, the morning market, the sake breweries, Hida beef, Hida Folk Village
Gero: footbaths, three public baths with a ¥1,300 pass, the Gassho Village, kaiseki and the New Year's Eve bell
Kyoto and Nara: Higashiyama and Kiyomizu-dera, Arashiyama, Fushimi Inari at dawn for whoever wants an early start, the National Museum on 2–3 Jan, Nara on 4 Jan
Hakone: the loop by ropeway, boat and shrine, the Open-Air Museum, a private bath, Fuji at dawn
Tokyo again: the Musée d'Orsay show, the National Museum open late on Fri 8 Jan, last shopping and last meals
plan.why: It is the only version that works for everyone. Every stay is two nights or more, no long move falls on a peak travel day, New Year's Eve has dinner included, and afternoons are kept light. Days can split: João and Carolina can do two big things a day while she and the parents do one.
plan.suits: Her at 29–32 weeks (beds, few moves, private baths), the parents on a first visit, and the first-timers (João, Carolina and Tatiana) who want the classic sights without exhaustion.
plan.trade: Gives up Okuhida's snow baths and Hiroshima. Both are a night more than the calendar allows.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus three full days. Jet lag and four first-timers need an easy start; Mon 21 Dec is a museum closing day, so it becomes the market-and-gardens day. One night less loses a whole side of the city.
stay_notes.kanazawa: Above the usual two or three days, deliberately: it is the slow stretch before New Year, it has the museums we care about, and everything must be done by Sun 27 Dec because museums close on Mon 28. A rental with a washing machine makes it the mid-trip reset.
stay_notes.takayama: The town fills one day and the Jinya closes on 29 Dec, so arrive about 13:30 on the 28th and see it that afternoon. One night more would buy the Okuhida ropeway and snow baths.
stay_notes.gero: Fixed by the calendar. Check in on 30 Dec, New Year's Eve at the ryokan, leave after the New Year breakfast on 1 Jan. One night would mean moving on 31 Dec, a peak travel day.
stay_notes.kyoto: Three big days plus Nara. Arrival on 1 Jan is late afternoon and counts as no day. Museums go on 2–3 Jan, Nara on Mon 4 Jan when Kyoto's museums close. One night less drops Nara or Arashiyama.
stay_notes.hakone: One full day for the loop and a museum, and two dawns for a clear Fuji. One night would make the ryokan a quick stopover with a single chance at Fuji.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: The museums that were closed in December, shopping, and a buffer before the flight. One night is possible but leaves no slack if a train or the weather slips.

tokyo.longer: A fifth night buys Kamakura or Nikko as a day trip. The city can fill any number of days.
tokyo.shorter: Three nights means two full days: one classic day is lost for the four first-timers, and the jet lag lands on a travel day.
tokyo.note: No idle risk. Tokyo fills every day, indoors or out.

kanazawa.longer: A fifth night (28 Dec) is a museum-closed Monday: the market and the castle park, or a Kaga Onsen half day. Mostly a rest.
kanazawa.shorter: Three nights squeezes Kenroku-en, the museums and the geisha district into two days and loses the slow day before New Year.
kanazawa.note: Day four (Sun 27 Dec) is light by design: the market, a workshop, laundry. Fine as a rest, dull if you want to be out all day.

takayama.longer: A third night buys Okuhida: the ropeway and the snow baths, a long cold day. Otherwise it is a second walk through the same old town.
takayama.shorter: One night would mean seeing the Jinya and the old town in one afternoon, then leaving; just possible, but rushed.
takayama.note: Day two (Tue 29 Dec) has the Jinya, Kyoya and two museums shut. The folk village and the breweries are open; it is a half day of things.

gero.longer: A third night is a day at the inn. Gero is a spa town, not a sight: footbaths, three public baths, a small folk village. Pleasant, not beautiful.
gero.shorter: One night means moving on 31 Dec, the busiest travel day of the year, and no quiet day before the New Year dinner.
gero.note: Be honest about this one: the second day in Gero is for the bath, a nap and the kaiseki. If idle days bother you, this is the stop to question. The alternative is New Year in Takayama or Kyoto.

kyoto.longer: A fifth night buys an easy day for Ohara or Kibune, or a second temple morning for the early risers.
kyoto.shorter: Three nights loses Nara or Arashiyama, because 1 Jan is an arrival afternoon and most places are shut until the 2nd.
kyoto.note: 1 Jan is a quiet arrival day with restaurants closed: the house, a convenience store, a walk. Expected, and the only such day here.

hakone.longer: A third night is a second chance at Fuji and a second museum day. Hakone has five museums, so a cloudy extra day is not wasted.
hakone.shorter: One night gives one morning for Fuji and no time for the loop; the ryokan becomes a stopover.
hakone.note: Two full mornings and one full day. On a cloudy day the museums fill it.

tokyo:2.longer: A third night at the end buys a Kamakura day or a proper last shopping day, and more slack before a Saturday flight.
tokyo:2.shorter: One night is enough for the flight, not for the museums that were shut in December.

gentle.tagline: One outing a day, then rest. The fewest check-ins of any version.
gentle.feel: The same opening in Tokyo, then four long stays and only four packing days. Kanazawa and Kyoto each get an extra night, so every day there holds one thing in the morning and nothing after lunch. Takayama becomes a four-night mountain base with New Year's Eve at a ryokan in the old town, and Okuhida or Shirakawa-go as unhurried day trips. Fuji is seen from the shinkansen or a Tokyo tower, or on an optional day trip from the last three Tokyo nights.
activities: Tokyo: the three classic days, spread over four nights
Kanazawa: Kenroku-en, the 21st Century Museum, the chaya districts, a crab lunch, and a free day
Takayama: the old town and market, Hida Folk Village, a slow Shirakawa-go day, an optional Okuhida snow day, New Year's Eve at a Takayama ryokan
Kyoto: Higashiyama, Arashiyama, Nara, and an easy day for Kibune or Ohara
Tokyo: museums, shopping, and Hakone as a day trip if anyone wants Fuji
gentle.why: Built around her and the parents: beds, few moves, private baths, and no day that needs stamina. The easiest pace for a 29–32 week pregnancy.
gentle.suits: Her, the parents, and anyone who would rather see less and never be tired.
gentle.trade: Gives up Hakone, the two Fuji dawns, and the onsen-town New Year's Eve. The first-timers see fewer places and João and Carolina may find it slow.

stay_notes.takayama: Four nights works at Gentle because the days stay half-empty: the old town, the folk village, Shirakawa-go and Okuhida as day trips, and New Year's Eve at a ryokan with dinner.
stay_notes.kyoto: Five nights gives a gentle day for Kibune or Ohara on top of the three big days and Nara.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Three nights at the end leave room for a Hakone day trip (about 80 minutes each way) or a rest day before the flight.

kanazawa.longer: There is nothing more to add; four nights already covers it with a rest day.
kanazawa.shorter: Three nights loses the rest day.
kanazawa.note: One free day is built in. Fine at a gentle pace.

takayama.longer: Nothing to add. Four nights is already generous for a one-day town.
takayama.shorter: Two nights loses the Shirakawa-go and Okuhida day trips and New Year in the old town.
takayama.note: Four nights in Takayama means two of the four days are day trips (Shirakawa-go, Okuhida) and 29–31 Dec have the museums shut. Without the day trips this is too long.

kyoto.longer: A sixth night is too many with the city half shut until 3 Jan.
kyoto.shorter: Four nights, as in the main route, loses the easy Ohara or Kibune day.
kyoto.note: 1 Jan is quiet by nature; the fifth day is a gentle one.

tokyo:2.shorter: Two nights loses the Hakone day trip and the rest day before the flight.
tokyo:2.note: Three nights at the end is easy to fill: museums, Kamakura, shopping.

full.theme: Everything, including the snow baths and Hiroshima
full.tagline: Eight bases, eight moves, two big things a day.
full.feel: A classic sightseeing trip. Tokyo and Kanazawa are trimmed to three nights, Okuhida's open-air baths in deep snow and the Shinhotaka ropeway go in between Takayama and Gero, and two Hiroshima nights with Miyajima follow Kyoto. The trade is time on trains: about 18 hours between bases, moves on 30 Dec and 4 Jan, one four-hour leg from Hiroshima to Hakone, and a single night in Tokyo at the end.
activities: Tokyo and Kanazawa in three nights each, two big things a day
Okuhida: rotenburo in the snow, the Shinhotaka ropeway to 2,156 m
Gero: the ryokan New Year's Eve
Kyoto in three nights, then Hiroshima's Peace Park and Miyajima's floating torii
Hakone's loop and Fuji, then one last Tokyo night
full.why: For the two who have been to Tokyo and Kyoto before, this is the version with six new places. It fits João and Carolina's wish to see a lot.
full.suits: João and Carolina. Pedro and Fernanda, for the new places.
full.trade: No rest days. Travel on the peak days 30 Dec and 4 Jan. A one-night stop at the end. Too tiring for her and probably for the parents.

stay_notes.okuhida: Two nights for the ropeway and the snow baths. New Year's Eve then falls in Gero after a 2-hour move on 30 Dec, a peak day.
stay_notes.hiroshima: Two nights: the Peace Park and museum on one day, Miyajima on the other. Then four hours to Hakone on 4 Jan, another peak day.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: One night. Enough for the flight, not for the museums.

tokyo.longer: Four nights gives the first-timers the third classic day.
tokyo.shorter: Two nights is too little for a first visit.
tokyo.note: Two big things a day; no idle risk, some tired legs.

kanazawa.longer: Four nights adds the rest day the main route has.
kanazawa.shorter: Two nights loses the museums or the geisha district.
kanazawa.note: Three nights is tight, not idle.

okuhida.longer: A third night is a second bath day in a hamlet with nothing else.
okuhida.shorter: A day trip from Takayama covers the ropeway and one bath without the move.
okuhida.note: Day two is the baths and the view. Beautiful, but there is nothing else to do; fine if a snow bath is the point.

hiroshima.longer: A third night buys Iwakuni or a second Miyajima evening.
hiroshima.shorter: One night means the Peace Park and Miyajima on the same day, which is a long day.

tokyo:2.longer: A second night buys the December museums back.

snow-monkeys.theme: The plan, with snow monkeys first
snow-monkeys.tagline: Two Nagano nights on the way to Kanazawa; the rest unchanged.
snow-monkeys.feel: Tokyo is cut to three nights and Kanazawa to three, which buys two nights in Yudanaka: wild macaques in a steaming pool in a snowy gorge, and Shibu Onsen's lantern-lit street of nine old public baths. It sits on the shinkansen line, so the detour is about 80 minutes to Nagano and a 40-minute bus. From there the trip runs exactly as the plan: Kanazawa, Takayama, Gero for New Year's Eve, Kyoto, Hakone, Tokyo.
activities: Yudanaka: the snow monkey park (a 30–40 minute forest walk on packed snow), Shibu Onsen's bath-hopping street, a ryokan dinner; Obuse's Hokusai museum on the way
Everything in the plan, with one day less in Tokyo and Kanazawa
snow-monkeys.why: Yudanaka is the one new place that adds something genuinely different at an easy pace, and it replaces nights rather than adding them.
snow-monkeys.suits: Anyone whose must-do is the snow monkeys. Works for the parents; she can wait at the ryokan if the path is icy.
snow-monkeys.trade: A Tokyo day and Kanazawa's fourth night, which was the rest day before New Year. Snow can be thin in late December.

stay_notes.yudanaka: Two nights: one for the monkeys, one for the onsen street. The forest path can be icy; cleats and a slow pace, or she stays at the ryokan.
stay_notes.tokyo: Three nights means two full days. The parents lose one classic day; it can be made up on 7–8 Jan.
stay_notes.kanazawa: Three nights means the museums day becomes a long one, or the Museum of Art drops out.

yudanaka.longer: A third night buys Nozawa or Zenko-ji; otherwise it is a second bath day.
yudanaka.shorter: One night makes the monkeys a rushed morning after a late arrival.
yudanaka.note: Day two is the bath street and a slow lunch. Lovely in snow, quiet without it.

tokyo.longer: Four nights gives back the classic day the first-timers lose here.
tokyo.shorter: Two nights is too little for a first visit.

kanazawa.longer: Four nights gives back the rest day.
kanazawa.shorter: Two nights loses the museums or the geisha district.
kanazawa.note: Three nights is full, not idle.

art-not-fuji.theme: Art islands and gardens instead of Fuji
art-not-fuji.tagline: Okayama replaces Hakone: Naoshima, Kurashiki, Korakuen and Himeji.
art-not-fuji.feel: Identical to the plan until Kyoto. Then an hour west to Okayama for two nights: Himeji Castle on the way (Tue 5 Jan, she stays in the grounds), Korakuen's New Year garden, Kurashiki's canal and the Ohara Museum, and a day on Naoshima for the Chichu Art Museum and Benesse House on Wed 6 Jan, when it is open. The ride back to Tokyo is three hours twenty on the Sanyo and Tokaido shinkansen.
activities: Himeji Castle, Japan's finest original keep
Korakuen, one of the three great gardens; Kurashiki's canal quarter and the Ohara Museum
Naoshima: Chichu Art Museum (timed tickets), Benesse House, the Yellow Pumpkin
Everything in the plan up to Kyoto
art-not-fuji.why: For a family that values museums and architecture, Naoshima is the strongest single addition. Flat towns suit her and the parents.
art-not-fuji.suits: The museum lovers. Those who have already seen Fuji.
art-not-fuji.trade: The Hakone ryokan with a private bath, and the two Fuji dawns. Island walking in a cold sea wind; Chichu is closed Mondays.

stay_notes.okayama: Two nights: Himeji on the way in and Korakuen or Kurashiki on 5 Jan, Naoshima on Wed 6 Jan (Chichu closed Mondays; Teshima closed Tue–Thu in winter). Then about 3 h 20 to Tokyo.

okayama.longer: A third night adds Kurashiki properly or Teshima if it is open.
okayama.shorter: One night loses Naoshima, which is the point.
okayama.note: Himeji on the way in, Naoshima on the full day. No idle risk if the ferry runs.

kinosaki.theme: Crab and seven baths instead of Fuji
kinosaki.tagline: Kinosaki Onsen replaces Hakone, in snow-crab season.
kinosaki.feel: Identical to the plan until Kyoto. Then 2 h 50 north-west to Kinosaki: a willow-lined canal town where everyone walks between seven public baths in yukata and geta, with a crab kaiseki at the ryokan. The town is flat, which suits the parents; she keeps to the ryokan's private bath because the public ones run hot. The catch is the way home: five to six hours back to Tokyo on 7 Jan.
activities: The seven public baths of Kinosaki, by yukata and geta
Snow-crab kaiseki at the ryokan, in season
The ropeway and Onsen-ji temple
Everything in the plan up to Kyoto
kinosaki.why: A classic onsen town at its best moment, for a family that liked the idea of the ryokan night and wants a second one.
kinosaki.suits: Onsen and crab lovers. Flat streets suit the parents.
kinosaki.trade: Hakone and Fuji, a 5–6 hour journey back to Tokyo, and it repeats Kanazawa's crab and Gero's onsen.

stay_notes.kinosaki: Two nights, the usual minimum for its New Year and crab-season plans. Book a ryokan with a private bath for her; the Nishimuraya houses have Western beds and a lift.

kinosaki.longer: A third night is a third evening of baths and crab in the same small town.
kinosaki.shorter: One night is a long way to go for one dinner.
kinosaki.note: Day two is the baths, the ropeway and the temple. Pleasant and slow; like Gero, the town is the inn.

fuji-lake.theme: Fuji across the lake instead of Hakone
fuji-lake.tagline: The postcard view from a lakeside ryokan; the rest of the plan unchanged.
fuji-lake.feel: Identical to the plan until Kyoto. Then the shinkansen to Mishima and the Fujikyu bus over the pass to Lake Kawaguchi, about four and a quarter hours door to door, an hour more than Hakone. The reward is the view: Fuji stands straight across the water, with nothing in the way, from the room, the bath, the north-shore promenade and the boat. One full day for the ropeway and the lake, a bowl of hoto noodles, and a dawn or two with the mountain pink. Then two hours on the Fuji Excursion train straight into Shinjuku for the last Tokyo days. Fuji shows fully on about six January mornings in ten.
activities: Oishi Park: the flat lakeside promenade with Fuji straight ahead, the easiest Fuji view of the trip for her
The Panoramic Ropeway and the lake boat: the big thing of the day
Chureito Pagoda for whoever wants an early start (398 steps), with the classic pagoda-and-Fuji shot
Hoto noodles at Hoto Fudou or Kosaku; footbaths on the north shore
The Itchiku Kubota kimono museum if it clouds over
Everything in the plan up to Kyoto, and the two Tokyo days after
fuji-lake.why: Pedro and Fernanda have done Hakone together. Kawaguchiko is new for everyone, and it has the better Fuji view: straight across the lake, not over a ridge. For a family that mostly wants the mountain, that is the point of the stay.
fuji-lake.suits: Anyone whose must-do is Fuji itself. Flat shoreline for her and the parents; the pagoda steps are optional.
fuji-lake.trade: Hakone's five museums for a cloudy day, the ryokan-with-private-bath culture of Hakone (lake hotels are more hotel than inn), and about an hour more on the way from Kyoto. On a cloudy day there is less to do.

stay_notes.kawaguchiko: Two nights, like Hakone: one full day for the ropeway and the lake, and two dawns to catch Fuji clear. Arrival from Kyoto is mid-afternoon, so day one is the promenade and the bath.

kawaguchiko.longer: A third night is a third chance at a clear Fuji and little else; the museums are small.
kawaguchiko.shorter: One night gives one dawn and no ropeway day.
kawaguchiko.note: On a cloudy day there is less to do than in Hakone: the kimono museum, the footbaths, hoto noodles. Clear days are full.
